about: The pass bars of the traversal audit. Every bar is a sentence of the movement study (reports/Hybrid character traversal study.md) or of its sourced notes, quoted word for word; tools/traversal/check_study.py proves each quote and each number is in that file. No bar may be written from memory or set by feel. LOCKED: this file and tests/audit.gd change only with Yasin's word (see study/README.md).

margin_rule.words: Where the study prints a range the bar is exactly that range; where its source notes give the measured spread the bar is that spread; a single figure with no spread anywhere passes within 10 % of it (Yasin's choice of three offered: 10 %, 5 %, no pass / fail).

walk_speed: Comfortable adult walking is about **1.27 to 1.46 m/s**
cadence: Young adults take 115 to 120 steps a minute with a 1.5 to 1.7 m stride (two steps)
stance60: In walking each foot is on the ground about 60 % of the cycle and in the air 40 %, with two short periods (10 to 12 % each) when both feet are down
stance62: the foot-down share falls to **62 % walking, 31 % running, 22 % sprinting**, and the both-feet-down period is replaced by a flight phase
switch: People switch from walk to run at about **2.0 m/s**
run_strides: Runners on a treadmill at 2.5, 3.5 and 4.5 m/s used strides of 1.86, 2.46 and 2.96 m
bob: The centre of mass rises and falls **2.7 to 4.8 cm** in walking, more at higher speed, while side-to-side sway shrinks from 7.0 to 3.9 cm as speed rises
run_bob: In running the bob is 8 to 9.5 cm
pelvis: about 3 degrees of tilt, 8.5 of side drop and 12 of rotation in total range
arms: Each arm swings with the opposite leg
elbows: Arms stay mostly straight in walking and bent in running
walk_joints: In walking the hip goes from 25 degrees of flexion to 10 of extension; the knee bends about 20 degrees as weight lands, straightens, is already 40 degrees bent at toe-off and peaks at 60 degrees in swing; the ankle goes from 10 degrees up to 20 degrees down
toe: The big toe must bend up at least 35 to 40 degrees at push-off
run_joints: Running roughly doubles swing-knee bend (94 to 119 degrees) and raises hip flexion from 44 to 61 degrees between 2.5 and 4.5 m/s, while the ankle barely changes
run_peaks: hip flexion 43.8° / 52.8° / 60.5°; hip extension 3.6° / 8.0° / 11.8°; knee flexion (swing) 93.5° / 108.7° / 119.1°; ankle dorsiflexion 26.4° / 26.5° / 26.8° (no speed effect); ankle plantarflexion 16.6° / 20.5° / 23.2°
run_width: stride length 1.86 / 2.46 / 2.96 m, cadence 80.8 / 85.7 / 91.7 strides/min, stride width 0.10 / 0.09 / 0.08 m
past_straight: elbows and knees barely go past straight: **elbow 0.8 to 4.7 degrees, knee 1.0 to 1.6 degrees** on average
head_first: People turn head first. On curved paths the eyes lead the pelvis by about 0.56 s and the head by 0.26 s, with the head turned about 15 degrees into the turn
head_sd: 264 ± 134 ms in light (269 ms and 129 ms in darkness); angular lead in light: gaze 27.5 ± 6.9°, head 14.8 ± 6.0°
circle: on a 1 m radius circle people chose 0.96 m/s against 1.61 m/s in a straight line
corner_lean: lean into a 90 degree corner by 4.4, 6.8 and 12.7 degrees at slow, normal and fast walking speed
spot: Turning 180 degrees on the spot takes about 3 to 4 steps, with the head, chest, pelvis and feet starting in that order and the head peaking at 137 to 272 degrees a second
start: A walk reaches about 90 % of its speed on the first step and steady speed in about three
stop_walk: A walk stops in under two steps, with the front leg stiffened and the rear foot left planted
stop_run: stopping from a flat-out run takes about **5 steps and 2.9 m**, with the body leaning back
standing: Quiet standing is never still: the pressure point under the feet drifts slowly, with a median sway frequency of about 0.33 Hz, and changes direction about every 0.2 s
stair_time: Stairs are climbed at about half a second per step: 0.51 s up and 0.47 s down
stair_joints: peak hip flexion is 62 degrees going up but only 21 going down, while the ankle bends 31 degrees going down against 18.5 going up
kerb: Stepping off a 14.6 cm kerb, people plant the last foot about 14 cm back from the edge
slope: Uphill the trunk tilts forward and the leg joints are more bent at foot contact; downhill the trunk tilts back
jump_rise: An average standing jump adds 0.41 to 0.50 m for men and a run-up typically 0.10 to 0.20 m more
jump_time: A natural standing jump spends 0.70 s dipping and 0.30 s pushing, and dipping deeper adds almost no height
drops: up to 0.30 m, step down in stride; 0.30 to 1.0 m, step or hop off with a soft landing; 1.0 to 2.0 m, a heavy landing or a turn, hang and drop
fold: Start the landing fold on the contact frame, since force peaks within 35 to 91 ms
drift: a planted foot drifts less than about 2 cm at steady walk and run
double_step: blending from walk to run shows no double step
three_steps: a full-stick start reaches walk speed in about three steps, not instantly
feet_fit: on the stairs and the 10 and 19 degree ramps both feet rest on the surface with no foot inside or floating above it by more than about 2 cm; knees never bend backward on any obstacle (step through frame by frame on the stairs); on flat ground turning IK on and off changes nothing visible; the head leads a turn and never passes its limit when the target goes behind
stage5: stopping from a walk takes one to two steps and from a run several, with no slide after the feet plant; a 180 degree turn on the spot takes about three steps; releasing and re-pressing the stick mid-stop recovers without a pop
look: Real turning uses 15 to 30 degrees of head lead, and the trunk does not lead at all. Share a look across spine, neck and head with most of the turn in the neck and almost none in the lower back, and cap head turn speed well under the 137 to 272 degrees a second measured for deliberate on-the-spot turns
lim_knee: hinge, 0 to about 140 degrees of bend; no visible back-bend (measured 1 to 2 degrees)
lim_hip: flexion about 130, extension about 17; spread 50, cross 30; twist 30 out and 40 in (hip extended)
lim_ankle: 13 up, 55 to 62 down; tilt 30 in, 20 out
lim_elbow: hinge, 0 to about 145 to 150; no back-bend (measured 1 to 5 degrees)
lim_shoulder: arm raise about 170; shoulder blade follows at about 1 degree per 2 of arm
lim_neck: 64 forward, 63 back, 49 side, 85 turn each way
lim_mid: 26 forward, 22 back, 30 side, 47 turn each way
lim_low: 65 forward, 31 back, 30 side, 15 turn each way
lim_wrist: bend 70 forward, 60 back; 20 toward thumb, 30 toward little finger; no twist
lim_forearm: about 77 to 82 palm-down, 85 to 91 palm-up; done by the forearm bones
lim_fingers: middle knuckle 100, end knuckle 80; grip pose about 61, 60, 39
lim_toe: 70 to 90 up expected; 35 to 40 needed for walking
lim_knee_twist: none when straight; at 90 degrees of bend, about 10 inward and 30 to 40 outward
crouch: crouch speed is about half walk speed
obstacle: Over a 12 to 17 cm obstacle the trailing foot is planted 18 to 26 cm before it, toes clear it by 11 to 19 cm, and speed drops from 1.23 to about 1.1 m/s
slope_limit: The right limit between is not given by any source in the notes; choose it in Stage 1 on the test ramp
